learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn to write highly economical and factual Classified ads, and visually engaging Commercial ads, targeting specific audiences within strict word limits.]
warm_up_hook: 📰 Whether you're selling a vintage bike or looking for a job, advertisements are the ultimate tool of persuasion. In the newspaper, every single word costs money! Let's learn how to be convincing and cheap at the same time! 💰

lesson_modules.module_title: 🗞️ Classified Ads: The Art of Economy
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Classified ads are text-heavy, factual, and printed in specific newspaper columns (e.g., Situation Vacant, To Let, For Sale, Missing). They are written in short phrases, not full sentences, to save space and money. They must always be in a box and have a category heading in CAPITALS.
examples_or_templates: Instead of: 'I have a car that I want to sell. It is a Honda City from 2019.'
Use: 'Available for sale a 2019 Honda City, silver-grey, excellent condition, single-owner...'

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Each classified type needs specific details. 'To Let' needs size, location, and rent expected. 'Situation Vacant' needs company name, qualifications required, and salary offered. 'For Sale' needs make, model, condition, and expected price.
examples_or_templates: To Let: 'Available 3BHK flat, East-facing, modular kitchen, parking...'
Situation Vacant: 'Wanted a dynamic receptionist, min 2 yrs experience, fluent in English...'

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Unlike classifieds, Commercial ads are designed for business promotion. They look like mini-posters. They use varying fonts, graphics, catchphrases, and highlight discounts, offers, or store locations to attract customers.
examples_or_templates: Features: 'Hurry! Flat 50% Off!', 'Buy 1 Get 1 Free', 'Visit our new showroom at...'

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Why are Classified Advertisements written in phrases instead of full, grammatically complete sentences?
options: Because grammar rules do not apply in newspapers.
To confuse the reader and make them call for details.
To save space, as classified ads are charged per word or line.
Because they are meant only for uneducated audiences.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: To save space, as classified ads are charged per word or line.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which heading is most appropriate if you are looking for a tenant for your empty apartment?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ You want to sell your old motorcycle. Draft a classified ad in 50 words.
subjective_practice.hint: Heading: FOR SALE. Include brand, year of manufacture, mileage, condition (e.g., 'scratchless'), expected price, and your contact number.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Your company needs a software engineer. Write a 'Situation Vacant' ad.
subjective_practice.hint: Mention the required degree, years of experience needed, key skills (e.g., Java, Python), and where to send the resume (email ID).

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Identify the missing element in this classified: 'Available a 2BHK flat in South Extension with modular kitchen and balcony. Rent negotiable.'
subjective_practice.hint: How will the interested person reach the owner? It's missing contact details (Phone number or email)!

activity_or_assignment.title: ✂️ The Word Shrinker
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Take the following paragraph and shrink it into a 30-word Classified Ad: 'Hello, my name is Raj. I am looking for a job as a math tutor. I have completed my MSc in Mathematics and I have been teaching for 5 years. I am willing to travel to students' homes in the North Delhi area. You can call me at 9876543210.'

chapter_summary: ⭐ Classified ads use category headings (e.g., FOR SALE, TO LET) and must be enclosed in a box.
⭐ Use short, comma-separated phrases to convey maximum information in minimum words (50-word limit).
⭐ Always conclude a classified ad with clear contact details (phone number, email, or P.O. Box).
